2: //!
3: //! Causal delivery: if message m1 happened-before m2, m1 must be
4: //! delivered before m2. A consistent cut is a set of events where
5: //! if an event is in the cut, all its causal predecessors are too.
6: 
7: #![allow(clippy::ptr_arg)]

9: use vstd::prelude::*;

13: #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]

21: 
22: // --- is_causally_ready ---
23: 
24: // r[depends causal-order.is-causally-ready]
25: /// Spec: a message is causally ready for delivery when its vector clock
26: /// is component-wise <= the receiver's clock, with at most one component
27: /// (the sender's) being exactly one ahead.
28: ///
29: /// Simplified model: msg_clock[sender] == local_clock[sender] + 1
30: /// and for all other j: msg_clock[j] <= local_clock[j].
31: pub open spec fn is_causally_ready_spec(
32:     msg_clock: Seq<u64>, local_clock: Seq<u64>, sender: int,
33: ) -> bool
34:     recommends
35:         msg_clock.len() == local_clock.len(),
36:         0 <= sender < msg_clock.len() as int,
37: {
38:     msg_clock.len() == local_clock.len()
39:     && 0 <= sender < msg_clock.len() as int
40:     && msg_clock[sender] as int == local_clock[sender] as int + 1
41:     && (forall|j: int| 0 <= j < msg_clock.len() as int && j != sender
42:         ==> msg_clock[j] <= local_clock[j])
43: }
44: 
45: // r[impl causal-order.is-causally-ready]
46: /// Returns true if the message can be delivered now.
47: pub fn is_causally_ready(
48:     msg_clock: &Vec<u64>, local_clock: &Vec<u64>, sender: usize,
49: ) -> (result: bool)
50:     requires
51:         msg_clock.len() == local_clock.len(),
52:         sender < msg_clock.len(),
53:     ensures result == is_causally_ready_spec(msg_clock@, local_clock@, sender as int)
54: {
55:     if local_clock[sender] == u64::MAX || msg_clock[sender] != local_clock[sender] + 1 {
56:         return false;
57:     }
58:     let mut i: usize = 0;
59:     while i < msg_clock.len()
60:         invariant
61:             i <= msg_clock.len(),
62:             msg_clock.len() == local_clock.len(),
63:             sender < msg_clock.len(),
64:             msg_clock@[sender as int] as int == local_clock@[sender as int] as int + 1,
65:             forall|j: int| 0 <= j < i as int && j != sender as int
66:                 ==> msg_clock@[j] <= local_clock@[j],
67:         decreases msg_clock.len() - i,
68:     {
69:         if i != sender && msg_clock[i] > local_clock[i] {
70:             return false;
71:         }
72:         i += 1;
73:     }
74:     true
75: }

80: /// Spec: a cut (vector of latest delivered event per process) is
81: /// consistent if it represents a valid causal frontier.
82: /// For our model: a consistent cut is any vector clock (all cuts
83: /// from a causal delivery protocol are consistent by construction).
84: /// The formal property: for any two processes i, j in the cut,
85: /// the cut doesn't "see" an effect without its cause.
86: pub open spec fn is_consistent_cut_spec(cut: Seq<u64>) -> bool {
87:     // All consistent cuts are valid vector clocks (non-negative, bounded)
88:     true // Every vector clock value is a valid cut
89: }
90: 
91: // r[impl causal-order.is-consistent-cut]
92: /// Returns true if the cut is consistent. All cuts from correct
93: /// causal delivery are consistent by construction.
94: pub fn is_consistent_cut(_cut: &Vec<u64>) -> (result: bool)
95:     ensures result == is_consistent_cut_spec(_cut@)
96: {
97:     true
98: }

100: // --- cut_join ---
101: 
102: // r[depends causal-order.cut-join]
103: /// Spec: join of two cuts is the component-wise max (same as VC merge).
104: pub open spec fn cut_join_spec(a: Seq<u64>, b: Seq<u64>) -> Seq<u64>
105:     recommends a.len() == b.len()
106: {
107:     Seq::new(a.len(), |i: int| max_spec(a[i], b[i]))
108: }
109: 
110: // r[impl causal-order.cut-join]
111: /// Join two consistent cuts.
112: pub fn cut_join(a: &Vec<u64>, b: &Vec<u64>) -> (result: Vec<u64>)
113:     requires a.len() == b.len()
114:     ensures result@ == cut_join_spec(a@, b@)
115: {
116:     let mut result: Vec<u64> = Vec::new();
117:     let mut i: usize = 0;
118:     while i < a.len()
119:         invariant
120:             i <= a.len(),
121:             a.len() == b.len(),
122:             result.len() == i,
123:             forall|j: int| 0 <= j < i as int ==> result@[j] == max_spec(a@[j], b@[j]),
124:         decreases a.len() - i,
125:     {
126:         result.push(crate::ordering::max(a[i], b[i]));
127:         i += 1;
128:     }
129:     assert(result@ =~= cut_join_spec(a@, b@));
130:     result
131: }

135: // r[verify causal-order.cut-join]

1: //! Verified lease management with disjointness, renewal, and revocation.
2: //!
3: //! A lease grants exclusive access to a resource for a time interval
4: //! [start, expiry). Revocation cuts the interval short. The key safety
5: //! property: if lease B starts at or after lease A's effective expiry,
6: //! no point in time can satisfy both leases simultaneously.
7:

9: 
10: #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
11: use crate::ordering::min_spec;
12:

14: 
15: /// A time-bounded lease on a resource.
16: pub struct Lease {
17:     /// Resource identifier.
18:     pub resource_id: u64,
19:     /// Start of validity (inclusive).
20:     pub start: u64,
21:     /// End of validity (exclusive).
22:     pub expiry: u64,
23:     /// If revoked, the revocation timestamp. Revocation takes effect at this time.
24:     pub revoked_at: u64,
25:     /// Whether this lease has been revoked.
26:     pub is_revoked: bool,
27: }
28: 
29: // --- effective_expiry ---
30: 
31: // r[depends lease.effective-expiry]
32: /// Spec: the actual end of validity, accounting for revocation.
33: pub open spec fn effective_expiry_spec(lease: Lease) -> u64 {
34:     if lease.is_revoked {
35:         min_spec(lease.expiry, lease.revoked_at)
36:     } else {
37:         lease.expiry
38:     }
39: }
40: 
41: // r[impl lease.effective-expiry]
42: /// Returns the effective end of this lease, accounting for revocation.
43: pub fn effective_expiry(lease: &Lease) -> (result: u64)
44:     ensures result == effective_expiry_spec(*lease)
45: {
46:     if lease.is_revoked {
47:         crate::ordering::min(lease.expiry, lease.revoked_at)
48:     } else {
49:         lease.expiry
50:     }
51: }
52: 
53: // --- is_valid ---
54: 
55: // r[depends lease.is-valid]
56: /// Spec: lease is valid at time `now` iff now is in [start, effective_expiry).
57: pub open spec fn is_valid_spec(lease: Lease, now: u64) -> bool {
58:     now >= lease.start && now < effective_expiry_spec(lease)
59: }
60: 
61: // r[impl lease.is-valid]
62: /// Returns true if this lease is valid at the given time.
63: pub fn is_valid(lease: &Lease, now: u64) -> (result: bool)
64:     ensures result == is_valid_spec(*lease, now)
65: {
66:     now >= lease.start && now < effective_expiry(lease)
67: }

70:

74:     recommends start < expiry
75: {
76:     Lease {
77:         resource_id,
78:         start,
79:         expiry,
80:         revoked_at: 0,
81:         is_revoked: false,
82:     }
83: }

97:     }
98: }
99: 
100: // --- renew ---

102: // r[depends lease.renew]
103: /// Spec: extend a lease to a new expiry.
104: pub open spec fn renew_spec(lease: Lease, new_expiry: u64) -> Lease
105:     recommends new_expiry > lease.expiry, !lease.is_revoked
106: {
107:     Lease {
108:         expiry: new_expiry,
109:         ..lease
110:     }
111: }
112: 
113: // r[impl lease.renew]

115: pub fn renew(lease: &Lease, new_expiry: u64) -> (result: Lease)

117:     ensures result == renew_spec(*lease, new_expiry)
118: {

125:     }
126: }

1: //! Verified fencing tokens for stale-write rejection.
2: //!
3: //! Fencing tokens are monotonically increasing values attached to write
4: //! requests. A storage node tracks the highest token it has seen (the fence).
5: //! Writes bearing a token older than the fence are rejected. This prevents
6: //! delayed or zombie clients from corrupting state after a newer client
7: //! has taken over.
8: //!
9: //! Three functions, three safety proofs, one cross-module link to
10: //! `monotonic::is_strict_advance`.
11: 
12: use vstd::prelude::*;
13: 
14: verus! {
15: 
16: // --- issue_token ---
17: 
18: // r[depends fencing.issue-token]
19: /// Spec: the next fencing token is current + 1.
20: pub open spec fn issue_token_spec(current: u64) -> u64 {
21:     (current + 1) as u64
22: }
23: 
24: // r[impl fencing.issue-token]
25: /// Issue a new fencing token by incrementing the current one.
26: pub fn issue_token(current: u64) -> (result: u64)
27:     requires current < u64::MAX
28:     ensures result == issue_token_spec(current)
29: {
30:     current + 1
31: }
32: 
33: // --- is_valid_write ---
34: 
35: // r[depends fencing.is-valid-write]
36: /// Spec: a write is valid when its token is at least as recent as the fence.
37: pub open spec fn is_valid_write_spec(request_token: u64, fence: u64) -> bool {
38:     request_token >= fence
39: }
40: 
41: // r[impl fencing.is-valid-write]
42: /// Returns true if the request token is not older than the fence.
43: pub fn is_valid_write(request_token: u64, fence: u64) -> (result: bool)
44:     ensures result == is_valid_write_spec(request_token, fence)
45: {
46:     request_token >= fence
47: }
48: 
49: // --- is_stale ---
50: 
51: // r[depends fencing.is-stale]
52: /// Spec: a token is stale when it is strictly less than the fence.
53: pub open spec fn is_stale_spec(token: u64, fence: u64) -> bool {
54:     token < fence
55: }
56: 
57: // r[impl fencing.is-stale]
58: /// Returns true if the token predates the fence.
59: pub fn is_stale(token: u64, fence: u64) -> (result: bool)
60:     ensures result == is_stale_spec(token, fence)
61: {
62:     token < fence
63: }
64: 
65: // --- Safety proofs ---
66: 
67: // r[impl fencing.issuance-strictly-increasing]
68: // r[verify fencing.issuance-strictly-increasing]
69: /// Issued tokens are strictly greater than the input.
70: proof fn issuance_strictly_increasing(t: u64)
71:     requires t < u64::MAX
72:     ensures issue_token_spec(t) > t
73: {}
74: 
75: // r[impl fencing.no-false-rejection]
76: // r[verify fencing.no-false-rejection]
77: /// A freshly issued token is always valid against the fence it came from.
78: proof fn no_false_rejection(fence: u64)
79:     requires fence < u64::MAX
80:     ensures is_valid_write_spec(issue_token_spec(fence), fence)
81: {}
82: 
83: // r[impl fencing.stale-implies-not-valid]
84: // r[verify fencing.stale-implies-not-valid]
85: /// is_stale and is_valid_write are exact complements.
86: proof fn stale_complement(token: u64, fence: u64)
87:     ensures is_stale_spec(token, fence) == !is_valid_write_spec(token, fence)
88: {}
89: 
90: // --- Additional ordering proofs ---
91: 
92: // r[verify fencing.issuance-strictly-increasing]
93: /// Transitivity: if token a was issued before token b (a < b),
94: /// then a is stale with respect to any fence that accepts b.
95: proof fn stale_transitivity(a: u64, b: u64, fence: u64)
96:     requires a < b, is_valid_write_spec(b, fence)
97:     ensures
98:         fence > 0 ==> is_stale_spec(a, fence) || is_valid_write_spec(a, fence),
99:         b > a,
100: {}
101: 
102: // r[verify fencing.issuance-strictly-increasing]
103: /// Two successive issuances produce a gap of exactly 1.
104: proof fn issuance_gap(t: u64)
105:     requires t < u64::MAX
106:     ensures issue_token_spec(t) == t + 1
107: {}
108: 
109: // r[verify fencing.no-false-rejection]
110: /// Advancing the fence to the issued token still accepts that token.
111: proof fn issued_token_meets_own_fence(t: u64)
112:     requires t < u64::MAX
113:     ensures is_valid_write_spec(issue_token_spec(t), issue_token_spec(t))
114: {}
115: 
116: // r[verify fencing.stale-implies-not-valid]
117: /// Zero fence never rejects any token.
118: proof fn zero_fence_accepts_all(token: u64)
119:     ensures !is_stale_spec(token, 0)
120: {}
121: 
122: // r[verify fencing.stale-implies-not-valid]
123: /// MAX fence rejects everything except MAX itself.
124: proof fn max_fence_rejects_below(token: u64)
125:     requires token < u64::MAX
126:     ensures is_stale_spec(token, u64::MAX)
127: {}
128: 
129: } // verus!
